subject.title: memory flush never triggers when reserveTokensFloor equals contextWindow

question: When `reserveTokensFloor + memoryFlush.softThresholdTokens` makes the memory-flush/preflight token threshold non-positive, should OpenClaw clamp the effective reserve, warn or validate config, or require a doctor migration for oversized existing configs?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the fix changes compatibility-sensitive config/default behavior and overlaps open budget-threshold PRs, so automation should not choose the product contract alone.

options.title: Centralize an effective positive threshold
options.body: Use one context-window-aware effective reserve/threshold path for memory flush and preflight compaction, then add focused regression coverage and docs for the chosen behavior.

options.title: Clamp only at memory-flush planning
options.body: Keep the fix local to `MemoryFlushPlan` resolution so the reported memory-flush bug is addressed without broad compaction-budget semantics changes.

options.title: Defer to a broader compaction-budget PR
options.body: Pause this issue until maintainers settle the adjacent reserve/soft-threshold PRs and then close or implement this bug through that canonical path.

recommendation.title: Centralize an effective positive threshold
recommendation.body: Use one context-window-aware effective reserve/threshold path for memory flush and preflight compaction, then add focused regression coverage and docs for the chosen behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue sits in the pre-compaction memory-flush feature and threshold policy that history most strongly associates with this owner path.
